current.text: James Harden is with Cleveland for the full season. The projected starting lineup is Harden, Mitchell, Peyton Watson, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen.
With Harden on the team last season, Mitchell's assists per 36 minutes fell from about 6.1 to about 5, an 18% drop. His usage fell from 32 to 30 and his scoring dropped 1.5 to 2 points.
For about two thirds of last season he played without Harden, with Darius Garland out or limited and with Max Strus out.

Experts expect fewer assists and less usage this season. One expert projects a 20 to 25% assist drop with Harden. Another projects just under 30% usage and 33 minutes. Peyton Watson will also take touches.
Last season he had his best two-point shooting ever, and he shot about 95% from the line in the second half. Experts expect his two-point percentage, free throw percentage and steals to come down.

How much he and Harden share the floor decides his value. A hard stagger would help him keep his value. Heavy shared minutes would hurt it. The bench has no clear point guard, so a stagger is possible.

Experts agree he is not a first-round pick in category leagues. A Yahoo rank around 14 is reasonable, but one expert would put him a bit lower. Another would take Jamal Murray and Austin Reaves ahead of him.
ESPN's rank 7 is far too high, and last season's top-10 finish is not likely to carry over. It is the only season he has played at that level.
In an auction mock draft he went for 31 USD, which the expert called about right.
Cleveland has the most back-to-backs in the league.
With our March 28 end, Cleveland plays 4, 3 and then 2 games in the fantasy playoffs. That means only two games in the finals week starting March 22.
He has no injury concerns now.
He signed a contract extension with Cleveland.
Cleveland is projected to win about 51 to 53 games.

durable.text: Points are his standout category and a real league outlier. He is also strong in threes, steals and FT%.
He has many turnovers for a guard.
FG% is not a strength. Two-point shooting has always been his weak point. His blocks and rebounds are also not strong.
For most of his career he has been a player ranked about 30 to 40.
He has had persistent knee problems, though he was fairly healthy last season.
He is 30 and has carried a heavy load over the last couple of years.

note: Experts agree he is not a first-round player with Harden there full time. They expect his assists, two-point shooting, free throws and steals to come down. That makes ESPN's 58 USD look too high and puts Yahoo's 46 USD at the top of his range. Our league paid 40 USD last season, and a recent mock took him at 31 USD, so aim for the low-to-mid 30s and fit him into a punt TO build. He gives big points, threes, steals and FT%. Early in the season, check how much he shares the floor with Harden, his assist rate, and how Cleveland's league-high back-to-backs affect his games. Also note the two-game finals week.
